title: Ananta Atrium — First-Person Campus for Live AI Agents
purpose: Executable plan for a browser-first, open-source 3D visualisation of live Ananta agents: avatars in a two-storey office building, several buildings in a walkable landscape.
goal: A polished hobby release: walk through a 3-bay campus, see ~50 agents with live state, stable 60 fps on a mid-range GPU, reproducible OSS build.
assumptions: Babylon.js is the renderer; no Three.js/Modoki runtime code is reused.
First-person is the only player mode before M4.
The collector runs on the same machine as the browser and Ananta.
llama.cpp exposes /slots and /metrics; if a field is missing the adapter degrades instead of failing.
Art style is archviz-realistic with baked lighting, not photoreal.
Target hardware: desktop browser with a mid-range dGPU or recent iGPU.
The Ananta hub (local Docker stack) requires authentication; the collector uses a dedicated token, never the browser.
llama.cpp runtimes in the Ananta stack are not guaranteed on port 8080; real ports come from stack config, not defaults.
open_questions: Which exact source provides per-agent identity and task text (Ananta hub API vs. OpenCode session API) — reference documented in AT-110, decision in AT-103.
Koota vs. a hand-written ECS for ~50 agents — resolved in AT-002.
Baked lightmaps vs. light probes for interiors — resolved in AT-206.

milestones.title: Foundation — walkable room with fake agents
milestones.description: Project skeleton, Babylon bootstrap, sim/render boundary, first-person controller, one room, three avatars with fake state.

milestones.title: Live data — Ananta agents drive the atrium
milestones.description: AgentState contract, Ananta integration reference, collector, Ananta hub/llama.cpp adapters, WebSocket stream, state→avatar mapping, offline handling.

milestones.title: One two-storey building
milestones.description: Modular blockout, stairs, navmesh, agent locomotion, rooms, interior occlusion and lighting, inspection UI.

milestones.title: Campus — buildings, landscape, 50 agents
milestones.description: Landscape, data-driven layout, streaming, LOD, outdoor culling, sky, navmesh stitching, crowd performance.

milestones.title: Product and open-source release
milestones.description: Menu/onboarding, settings, audio, UI polish, accessibility, docs, licence, CI, release pipeline, perf budgets.

milestones.title: Stretch — after the release
milestones.description: Activity replay, spectator mode, touch controls, localisation. Only after M0–M4 are done.

tasks.title: Bootstrap the project skeleton
acceptance_criteria: npm run dev starts Vite and serves a Babylon canvas at localhost.
npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test and npm run build all pass on a clean checkout.
TypeScript strict is enabled; ESM only; Node 24 pinned in .nvmrc and package.json engines.
Directory layout matches AGENTS.md (src/sim, src/render, src/world, src/net, src/app, src/shared, collector, tests, devtools, todos).
An import-boundary check exists that fails if src/sim imports @babylonjs/*.
tasks.notes: Scaffold, scripts, .nvmrc, ESM/strict, boundary gate and test setup land in the repo.

tasks.title: Babylon scene bootstrap and frame loop
acceptance_criteria: Engine prefers WebGPU and falls back to WebGL2 automatically; the active API is logged once.
Resize, devicePixelRatio and canvas focus are handled without distortion or blur.
A fixed-step simulation tick is decoupled from the render loop and exposes an interpolation alpha.
Dev-only Inspector can be toggled with a key and is excluded from production builds.
The render loop keeps running when the tab is backgrounded, but the sim can pause (documented behaviour).
tasks.notes: Vite + Babylon bootstrap with WebGPU attempt and WebGL2 fallback; fixed-step frame loop in src/app/session.ts.

tasks.title: Decide and enforce the sim/render boundary
acceptance_criteria: An ADR (docs/adr/0001-simulation-boundary.md) records the decision: koota vs. hand-written ECS vs. plain systems.
src/sim runs a complete tick headlessly in Vitest with no DOM and no Babylon import.
The ESLint zone / dependency check fails on a deliberate reverse import and this is proven by a test.
The chosen approach is validated at 50 agents in a micro-benchmark (tick cost recorded).
tasks.notes: Hand-written sim store (no Koota); boundary enforced by devtools/check-sim-boundary.mjs and documented in docs/architecture.md.

tasks.title: First-person character controller
acceptance_criteria: WASD + mouse look + sprint + jump, with pointer lock and a clear release path (Esc).
Havok character controller climbs steps up to 0.22 m and refuses slopes above 45 degrees.
Player cannot clip through walls at sprint speed when running diagonally into corners.
Camera height matches eye level (~1.7 m) and does not jitter on stairs.
Key bindings are read from config, not hard-coded at call sites.
tasks.notes: Pointer-lock first-person controller with gravity, collisions and stair ramps (src/app/controller.ts).

tasks.title: Room blockout and collision
acceptance_criteria: One 8x8 m room with 3 m ceiling and one door opening, authored in metric units.
Static colliders match the visible geometry within 5 cm.
Player can enter and leave through the door but not through walls.
Scale reference: a 1.8 m capsule stands correctly next to the door frame.
tasks.notes: Three two-storey buildings from scene.json: slabs, corridor walls with door gaps, stair ramps, collisions.

tasks.title: Agent avatar rendering
acceptance_criteria: Three avatars render (capsule placeholder or GLB) with a name label and a status colour ring.
Labels are readable at 10 m without overlapping the model; they face the camera.
Status colour palette is defined in one place and documented.
Rendering three avatars costs under 1 ms CPU per frame in the reference scene.
tasks.notes: Capsule/head/beacon/ring avatars synced from AgentState.position with status colours.

tasks.title: Agent state model and deterministic fake source
acceptance_criteria: AgentState v1 TypeScript type lives in src/shared with a matching JSON Schema.
A seeded fake source produces stable, reproducible sequences of states for three agents.
Switching a fake agent between idle/thinking/tool_use/waiting changes its visual within one tick.
Fake data is always labelled as fake in the debug HUD.
tasks.notes: AgentState v1 schema/types plus deterministic seeded fake simulation; no Math.random and no wall-clock state.

tasks.title: Debug HUD and developer toggles
acceptance_criteria: HUD shows fps, frame ms, draw calls, triangles, agent count and active data source (fake/live).
HUD is toggled with F3 and never ships enabled by default.
Turning the HUD off restores the previous render state (no leftover DOM overlay).
tasks.notes: Babylon GUI HUD: source badge, fps/tick/backend, room, nearest-agent panel; F2 toggles avatars.

tasks.title: M0 end-to-end smoke test
acceptance_criteria: Playwright boots the built app headlessly, enters pointer lock, walks forward and asserts movement.
The test asserts that three avatar labels are visible and that the HUD reports source=fake.
Test runs in CI and fails the build on a red result.
tasks.notes: Playwright smoke test boots the app, asserts 50 fake agents, walking and a live render loop.

tasks.title: Record the M0 performance baseline
acceptance_criteria: docs/perf-baseline.md lists GPU/CPU, resolution and measured draw calls, triangles, frame ms.
Budget thresholds for M2 and M3 are written down as numbers.
Method is reproducible (same scene, same camera path, same build mode).
tasks.notes: Headless baseline, budgets and the reproducible perf harness are committed; a reference-GPU run is still external (docs/perf-baseline.md).

tasks.title: Define the AgentState v1 contract
acceptance_criteria: JSON Schema in src/shared/agent-state.schema.json with version, id, status, room, task and timestamps.
Collector and client both validate against the schema in tests.
Unknown optional fields are preserved, not silently dropped.
Breaking changes require a version bump and a migration note.
tasks.notes: src/shared/agent-state.schema.json + strict TypeScript contract; both simulated and collector states validate in tests.

tasks.title: Document the Ananta integration reference
acceptance_criteria: docs/integration-ananta.md names the Ananta repository, the Docker compose project, the hub base URL and the exact task/agent/event endpoints the collector consumes.
The hub authentication flow is documented end to end (token source, header, required role/scope) with a working example request against the local stack.
The live event contract (SSE /events/stream and /api/tasks/<id>/control-state) is written down with field-level mapping to AgentState, including gaps.
llama.cpp endpoints used for metrics are listed with the real host ports from the Ananta stack config, not assumed defaults such as 8080.
README.md links the document and no longer refers to 'the Ananta stack' without a concrete pointer.
tasks.notes: docs/integration-ananta.md covers repo, compose stack, hub URL/auth, sessions/tasks/control-state, SSE, llama ports and the spectator admin flow.

tasks.title: Collector service skeleton
acceptance_criteria: Node/TypeScript service with env-based config and no hard-coded ports/URLs.
GET /health returns status, version, upstream reachability and last successful poll.
Structured JSON logs; graceful shutdown closes sockets and timers.
Unit tests cover config parsing and health output.
Hub base URL and agent token come from env; a missing or rejected token is reported as an upstream auth failure in GET /health, never masked as an empty state stream.
tasks.notes: Node/TS collector with env config, /health, JSON logs, graceful shutdown and unit tests.

tasks.title: llama.cpp adapter (slots, metrics, health)
acceptance_criteria: Polls /health, /props and /slots at a configurable interval with timeouts and backoff.
Maps busy/idle slots and token rates onto agent activity without inventing tasks.
Missing endpoints or fields degrade to 'unknown' and are logged, never crash the collector.
Recorded fixtures cover healthy, slow, 404 and malformed responses.
tasks.notes: llama.cpp /slots adapter computes throughput deltas and degrades to zero without throwing.

tasks.title: Session/agent adapter for identity and task text
acceptance_criteria: A documented source provides stable agent identity and current task; primary candidate is the Ananta hub API (task control-state plus SSE events), with OpenCode session events as fallback.
Mapping from raw events to AgentState is documented with examples.
Adapter is optional and pluggable; without it the collector still reports llama.cpp activity.
No secrets, prompts or user content leave the local machine; only the documented fields are published.
tasks.notes: Ananta hub adapter reads /api/sessions and /api/tasks, maps statuses and assigns deterministic desks.

tasks.title: Normalized state hub and WebSocket broadcast
acceptance_criteria: Hub merges adapters into one snapshot plus deltas at 5-10 Hz with coalescing/backpressure.
WebSocket clients receive a snapshot on connect and deltas afterwards.
50 concurrent clients do not increase per-client CPU beyond a documented budget.
Integration test drives the hub with fixtures and asserts snapshot/delta consistency.
tasks.notes: Snapshot on connect, coalesced deltas, heartbeat, backpressure (1 MB bufferedAmount) and a 50-client CPU test.

tasks.title: Client WebSocket layer with fake fallback
acceptance_criteria: Reconnect with exponential backoff and heartbeat; no unhandled promise rejections.
After disconnect the client switches to the fake source within 2 s and labels it in the HUD.
On reconnect the client resumes without a page reload and flags the source as live again.
Unit tests cover disconnect, timeout, malformed frame and reconnect.
The browser never receives the Ananta agent token; any collector-issued stream credential is short-lived and scoped to the collector WebSocket.
tasks.notes: Reconnect with exponential backoff, malformed-frame guard, 2 s labelled fake fallback; unit tests cover close, timeout and malformed frames.

tasks.title: Map AgentState onto avatar visuals
acceptance_criteria: A documented table maps status → animation/colour/label text for every status value.
Transitions complete within 150 ms and never rest in a T-pose.
Unknown status renders a neutral, clearly marked visual instead of throwing.
Visual mapping is data-driven (one config object), not scattered switch statements.
tasks.notes: Agent visuals driven by status, activity, position, stale and source.

tasks.title: Deterministic desk and room assignment
acceptance_criteria: An agent id always maps to the same desk across reloads and collector restarts.
Two agents never occupy the same desk; overflow is visible in the debug HUD.
Assignment is data-driven (desk list per room) and testable without Babylon.
tasks.notes: Deterministic desk assignment shared by sim and collector; duplicate-free in tests.

tasks.title: Staleness and offline handling
acceptance_criteria: Agents unseen for >30 s are visually stale; >5 min are shown as offline.
Thresholds live in config and are documented.
Stale agents never keep animating 'thinking' as if live.
tasks.notes: Stale flags, offline status, collector health degradation and client fallback; never presented as live.

tasks.title: M1 acceptance test with live Ananta
acceptance_criteria: With Ananta running, at least five agents update without a page reload.
Killing the collector shows the fake fallback within 2 s; restarting resumes live data.
Scenario is automated where possible and documented as a manual checklist where not.
tasks.notes: Automated fallback/adapter coverage and docs/manual-live-checklist.md exist; the live run needs ATRIUM_HUB_TOKEN and role scope.

tasks.title: Two-storey building blockout
acceptance_criteria: Two floors, two staircases, one corridor, at least six offices and one meeting room.
All rooms are reachable on foot from the entrance; dimensions are documented.
A metrics table lists floor heights, room sizes, door widths and stair pitch.
Blockout uses modular pieces (wall/floor/door/stair) rather than unique meshes.
tasks.notes: Two-storey blockout with slabs, stair openings, corridors, rooms and roof.

tasks.title: Tune the controller for stairs and doors
acceptance_criteria: Both staircases are climbed and descended without jumping or falling through.
Door thresholds and ramps up to 0.22 m are traversed smoothly.
Behaviour is verified at walk and sprint speed on both floors.
tasks.notes: Analytic stair zones plus door gaps; Playwright climbs and descends the atrium staircase in both directions.

tasks.title: Navmesh and agent pathfinding
acceptance_criteria: A navmesh is generated per floor and connected via stair links.
Agents can path between every pair of rooms; unreachable targets fail with an explicit reason.
A debug view renders the navmesh and current paths.
Path computation for 50 agents stays within the recorded budget.
tasks.notes: Per-floor walkable grid navmesh (0.5 m cells, door-aware) plus graph pathing, explicit failure reasons, F3 debug view and a 50-path budget test.

tasks.title: Agent locomotion and animation states
acceptance_criteria: Idle, walk, type-at-desk and meeting states exist and blend smoothly.
Movement speed matches the gait; turning happens in place at corners.
Foot sliding stays below a documented threshold at normal speed.
Agents never walk through walls or each other's desks.
tasks.notes: Idle/walk/type/meeting states, procedural limbs, speed-matched gait and LOD; no skeletal rig yet, documented in ADR 004.

tasks.title: Room system with occupancy queries
acceptance_criteria: Rooms have stable ids, names and a type (office, meeting, corridor, social).
Door portals are defined and used for transitions.
API answers 'which agents are in room X' and 'which room contains point P'.
Room membership is visible in the debug overlay.
tasks.notes: Stable room/corridor ids and kinds, door portals, occupancy API, point query and room counts in the agent list/minimap.

tasks.title: Interior occlusion and culling
acceptance_criteria: Rooms that are not visible through a door/portal are culled.
Draw calls drop by at least 40% versus the naive whole-building render on the reference camera path.
No visible popping when walking through doors; measured on a recorded path.
Culling state is inspectable in the debug HUD.
tasks.notes: Room-portal culling with 51-79% fewer draw calls vs naive, HUD counters and a perf gate.

tasks.title: Interior lighting with baked light
acceptance_criteria: Interiors use baked lightmaps or light probes; no realtime shadow maps indoors.
Exposure is consistent between rooms and near windows.
Lighting cost is measured and within the M2 budget.
Decision (lightmaps vs. probes) is recorded in an ADR.
tasks.notes: Per-room light probes (window/floor), no realtime shadow maps, ADR 003 and measured cost in the perf baseline.

tasks.title: Material and asset pipeline
acceptance_criteria: Documented glTF + PBR import path with deterministic asset hashes.
KTX2 textures are used when available and fall back to PNG/WebP without breaking.
Every asset has a row in ATTRIBUTION.md with source and licence.
A broken/missing asset fails loudly at load, not with an invisible mesh.
tasks.notes: Manifest with hashes/licences, KTX2->WebP->PNG fallback, glTF path, loud failures, check:assets and tests; docs/assets.md.

tasks.title: Agent inspection UI
acceptance_criteria: Hover highlights an agent; click opens a panel with name, status, task, room and last update.
Optional follow-camera mode can be toggled and exits cleanly with Esc.
Panel works with keyboard only and traps focus correctly.
No layout shift when the panel opens/closes.
tasks.notes: Nearest-agent inspection panel shows name, role, task, progress, throughput and source.

tasks.title: M2 acceptance — one building end to end
acceptance_criteria: A scripted agent walks desk → staircase → meeting room on floor 2 without getting stuck.
The walk is automated (test or recorded replay) and reproducible.
The player can follow the same path at 60 fps on the reference hardware.
tasks.notes: Automated desk->stairs->first-floor meeting walk test plus interactive inspection panel.

tasks.title: Campus landscape
acceptance_criteria: Walkable terrain with paths, props and collision; no floating or intersecting props.
Ground materials tile without visible seams at player eye height.
A documented measurement of the walkable area and the walk time between buildings.
Terrain and props use LODs or instancing where repeated.
tasks.notes: Five buildings, plaza, paths, instanced trees/desks, collision and documented walk times (docs/campus.md).

tasks.title: Data-driven campus layout
acceptance_criteria: scene.json lists buildings, transforms, entrances and nav links.
Adding a building requires only data, no code change (proven by adding a third building).
Invalid layout data fails validation with a path-specific error.
Schema for the layout file is documented.
tasks.notes: Campus layout, rooms, desks and outdoor nodes live in src/world/scene.json and are validated at load.

tasks.title: AssetContainer streaming
acceptance_criteria: Buildings load and unload by distance with hysteresis; no thrashing at the boundary.
No frame hitch above 16 ms during a load on the reference path.
GPU/CPU memory returns to baseline after unloading (measured).
Streaming state is visible in the debug HUD.
tasks.notes: Distance streaming with 70/95 m hysteresis; pre-built meshes mean no load hitch and memory stays at baseline (ADR 005).

tasks.title: LOD strategy for buildings, props and avatars
acceptance_criteria: LOD levels and switch distances are documented per asset class.
Visual popping is acceptable on the recorded camera path (reviewed).
Draw-call and triangle budgets are met or the numbers are documented as a known deviation.
tasks.notes: Avatar three-step LOD, room culling for interior detail, documented thresholds (docs/lod.md).

tasks.title: Outdoor culling
acceptance_criteria: Frustum, distance and occlusion culling are active outdoors.
Campus draw calls stay below the documented budget on the reference path.
CPU and GPU timings per pass are recorded in docs/perf-baseline.md.
tasks.notes: Frustum + room-portal + distance culling outdoors; draw calls and timings in docs/perf-baseline.md.

tasks.title: Sky and exterior lighting
acceptance_criteria: HDRI sky and sun lighting are consistent with interior exposure.
Entering a building does not flash or jump in exposure.
Optional time-of-day changes are smooth and documented.
tasks.notes: Procedural gradient sky dome, sun/hemisphere/fill lights, fog and light probes with no exposure jumps.

tasks.title: Stitch indoor and outdoor navigation
acceptance_criteria: Outdoor navmesh connects to every building entrance.
Agents traverse inside ↔ outside without teleporting or sticking at the seam.
Unreachable building/room combinations are reported explicitly.
A recorded agent walk crosses at least two buildings.
tasks.notes: Graph and grid connect every building gate to the plaza; cross-building paths tested; unreachable targets return explicit reasons.

tasks.title: 50-agent crowd performance
acceptance_criteria: 50 agents render at 60 fps on the reference dGPU and at least 30 fps on the reference iGPU.
Sim tick cost for 50 agents is measured and within budget.
Crowd technique (instancing, VAT or skinned clones) is decided in an ADR with measured numbers.
No GC spikes above the documented threshold during a 5-minute run.
tasks.notes: 50 agents run and walk; sim tick and path budgets are tested, crowd ADR written. Reference dGPU/iGPU fps still needs hardware.

tasks.title: M3 acceptance — campus walkthrough
acceptance_criteria: A 5-minute recorded walkthrough across the campus runs without a hitch above the threshold.
Memory is stable across the walk (no monotonic growth).
Performance check runs in CI or nightly with a stored baseline.
All five buildings are reachable and enterable.
tasks.notes: Five-building walkthrough, culling and memory checks run in Playwright; the 5-minute reference-hardware run remains external.

tasks.title: Main menu and onboarding
acceptance_criteria: First run offers 'connect to Ananta' and 'demo mode', with the difference explained.
Connection settings are remembered; a failed connection explains what to check.
A new user reaches a walkable scene in under 60 seconds in demo mode.
Menu is keyboard navigable and works at 720p and 4K.
tasks.notes: Menu with demo/connect explanation, persisted collector URL, error guidance and a keyboard-only path into the scene.

tasks.title: Settings and persistence
acceptance_criteria: Graphics quality, key bindings and audio volumes are configurable and persisted.
Settings apply without a reload where technically possible; otherwise the reload is explicit.
Reset-to-defaults exists and works.
Invalid stored settings fall back safely and are logged.
tasks.notes: Quality, key bindings, audio, language, UI scale, motion/colour settings persisted locally; reset and safe fallback tested.

tasks.title: Audio pass
acceptance_criteria: Ambience, footsteps and status cues exist and can be muted independently.
No autoplay violation: audio starts only after a user gesture.
Audio assets are attributed and licensed.
Spatial audio is used where it helps orientation, with a documented fallback.
tasks.notes: Procedural ambience, footsteps and status cues via Web Audio after a gesture, independent volumes, stereo pan.

tasks.title: UI and UX polish
acceptance_criteria: Agent list with filter by status/room, minimap and tooltips are implemented.
All interactive elements are reachable by keyboard and have visible focus.
Visual style is consistent (one spacing/colour/type scale).
No text smaller than 12 px at 1080p.
tasks.notes: Agent list with status/room filters and occupancy counts, minimap, tooltips, focus styles, one type/spacing scale.

tasks.title: Accessibility
acceptance_criteria: Reduced-motion mode, colour-blind-safe status palette and scalable UI text.
Status is never communicated by colour alone (icon or label too).
A documented manual accessibility checklist is completed.
Keyboard-only playthrough of the core loop is possible.
tasks.notes: Reduced motion, colour-blind palette, status icons+labels, scalable text and keyboard playthrough; manual SR/contrast/Safari checks remain.

tasks.title: README, screenshots and play link
acceptance_criteria: README has a one-paragraph pitch, screenshot/GIF, play link and a <10-line setup.
Architecture summary links to AGENTS.md and the ADRs.
Contributor entry point is obvious (CONTRIBUTING, good first issues).
All screenshots show the current build.
tasks.notes: README with screenshots, setup, scripts and architecture links; Pages deploy workflow provided.

tasks.title: Licence, attribution and contributing
acceptance_criteria: LICENSE for code (BSD-3-Clause) is present and referenced from README.
ATTRIBUTION.md lists every third-party asset with source and licence.
CONTRIBUTING.md explains setup, checks, PR rules and the task-id convention.
CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md exists.
No asset with an incompatible licence remains in the repo.
tasks.notes: BSD-3-Clause LICENSE, ATTRIBUTION.md and CONTRIBUTING.md added; no third-party art assets.

tasks.title: CI pipeline
acceptance_criteria: CI runs typecheck, lint, unit tests, e2e tests, build and todo validation.
Required checks block merge to main.
Build artifact is deployable to a static host (GitHub Pages or itch.io).
Node version is pinned to the same version as local development.
tasks.notes: CI runs boundary/typecheck/lint/i18n/assets/tests/build/e2e/todo validation; artefact deploy workflow. Branch protection is a repo setting.

tasks.title: Release pipeline and versioning
acceptance_criteria: Semantic versioning, CHANGELOG and tagged releases.
A release produces a versioned static bundle with a persistent URL.
Rollback to the previous release is documented and tested once.
Build is reproducible from a clean checkout at the tag.
tasks.notes: SemVer check, CHANGELOG, release workflow, versioned zip, Pages deploy, rollback doc and a byte-identical double build.

tasks.title: Performance regression budget in CI
acceptance_criteria: A reference scene and camera path are rendered in CI/nightly with recorded frame ms and draw calls.
A regression above the documented threshold fails the check.
Flaky results are handled (median of N runs, documented variance).
Results are published as an artifact or comment.
tasks.notes: Nightly perf workflow with medians, committed baseline, 35% regression gate and uploaded results artifact.

tasks.title: Agent activity replay
acceptance_criteria: Agent events are journaled with timestamps and can be replayed deterministically.
A scrubber moves through a recorded session.
Replay works offline without the collector.
tasks.notes: Snapshot journal with timestamps, scrubber, play/pause/live and offline replay; unit tests for seek/serialisation.

tasks.title: Spectator mode
acceptance_criteria: A second client observes the same session without controlling it.
State sync stays under 200 ms on a local network.
Host can revoke a spectator.
tasks.notes: Read-only spectator URL, collector spectator tracking, admin-token revocation endpoint and an e2e revocation test. State rate is 8 Hz (<125 ms).

tasks.title: Touch controls
acceptance_criteria: Virtual joystick and look area work on mobile Chrome and Safari.
No stuck inputs after multi-touch or backgrounding.
Touch UI can be disabled and never appears on desktop.
tasks.notes: Joystick/look area, auto policy, reset on blur/hide and touch e2e; real iOS Safari test still manual.

tasks.title: Localisation (de/en)
acceptance_criteria: All UI strings are externalised into locale files.
Language switch is persisted and applies without a reload.
No hard-coded user-facing string remains in components (lint check).
tasks.notes: en/de dictionaries with parity check, persisted switch without reload and a lint gate against literal UI strings.

execution_stage_summary.note: Nothing started yet. Begin with AT-000, then AT-002 (boundary) before feature work.

summary_notes: M0 is a hard gate: if walking and fake agents do not feel right, the campus will not fix it.
AT-307 (50-agent crowd performance) is the highest-risk item; reduce agent count before adding complexity.
The sim/render boundary (AT-002) is the one rule that must never be relaxed.
Every completed task needs evidence, not just a status change.
